channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
item.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.

item.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
item.description: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

item.title: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos
item.description: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.

item.title: NPR's Senior Podcast Challenge: Early entries we love
item.description: People 65 and older have been submitting stories for a chance to win our grand prize — a visit to NPR watch your podcast air live on Weekend Edition . There's still time to enter!

item.title: He expected a small-business loan. It turned out to be a trap
item.description: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost.

item.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
item.description: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

item.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
item.description: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.

item.title: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI
item.description: NATO officials and defence experts gathered at the NATO Edge conference in Turkey this week to discuss how militaries can harness artificial intelligence and high tech without compromising control over sensitive data and defence capabilities.

item.title: Multiple people shot at 'large' party in California, sheriff's office says
item.description: Officials said a call about a shooting in Strathmore came in at about 7:40 p.m.

item.title: Meet the Ukrainian energy workers dodging drones to bring people's electricity back
item.description: "The first thing the guys and I do is look at where we can hide."

item.title: Wash. officials condemn ICE after 2 arrested boarding flight at Seattle airport
item.description: Plainclothes officers in masks detained two people who were boarding a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

item.title: Live: At least 14 feared trapped after Russian strike in Kyiv region, Zelensky says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at least 14 people were missing after a Russian drone struck a five-story residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, injuring two others. Meanwhile, Finland warned the war was "spilling over" after a drone set fire to a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
item.description: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.

item.title: FBI's national crime database targeted in hack, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center database was targeted in a hack.

item.title: Britain's next fighter jet could be last with a pilot in the cockpit, says RAF chief
item.description: Britain's next fighter jet could be the last to fly with a pilot in the cockpit, according to the head of the RAF.

item.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.

item.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
item.description: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.

item.title: At least 24 dead after boat taking passengers to funeral capsizes in Nigeria
item.description: At least 24 people have died after a boat capsized carrying people to a funeral in Nigeria, according to emergency services.

item.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
item.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

item.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
item.description: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.

item.title: Hotel Chocolat recalls several Christmas boxes over potential salmonella risk
item.description: Several different sizes of Christmas boxes by Hotel Chocolat have been recalled due to a potential risk of salmonella in pistachios.

item.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draw lower turnout
item.description: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.

item.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
item.description: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations. Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting. France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.

item.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
item.description: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

item.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
item.description: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

item.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
item.description: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

item.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

item.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
item.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.

item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

item.title: FBI criminal database hacked
item.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
item.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

item.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
item.description: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020. It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.

item.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

item.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
item.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

item.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
item.description: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

item.title: New day of protests across France
item.description: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

item.title: Mexico captures drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after deadly firefight
item.description: Mexico's military forces captured ​one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," the military announced on Saturday, after a deadly firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers. Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City after his capture.

item.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
item.description: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

item.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: Prosecutors argued the defendant, 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht, had been "mad at everything" in the days leading up to the January 2025 fire, which killed 12 people.

item.title: At least 11 dead after suspected cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in Mexico
item.description: An outburst of violence has killed at least 11 people after Mexican authorities captured suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro.

item.title: German bidder stages last-gasp bid to rescue Poundland
item.description: A German investment firm has made a last-minute entry into the race to save Poundland, just days before its directors face the bleak prospect of appointing administrators to one of Britain's biggest high street retailers.

item.title: Denmark says it thwarted 'Russian plot' to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Police thwarted a Russian plot to kill a US-Ukrainian rapper who was performing in Denmark, according to authorities.

item.title: Administration tries to intervene after Kalshi is threatened with restraining order
item.description: The Trump administration tried to step in after Kalshi warned it could be crippled if a judge grants a temporary restraining order being sought by the New York AG.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for hosting Friendsgiving this year
item.description: Digital creator Kerra Masella shares her tips for planning and hosting a Friendsgiving celebration, from getting organized ahead of time to making friends feel welcome around the table.

item.title: USDA hit with cyberattack: Sources
item.description: One system affected is a tool for farmer payments, a source said.

item.description: Katy Nastro, travel correspondent at Flighty, shares what travelers can do to protect themselves.

item.title: Trump touts relationships with Putin and Xi after historic Asia trip
item.description: Trump said the three countries made strides in advancing denuclearization talks.

item.title: WATCH: New health warning on doomscrolling: What to know and tips to break the habit
item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.description: President Donald Trump says U.S. tech companies will face “a tremendous tax” if they build artificial intelligence data centers in other countries

item.title: WATCH: Reporter goes undercover as porch pirate
item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.title: White House replaces national cyber director amid widespread tech outages
item.description: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross has been fired, according to a source close to the White House.

item.title: Anthropic among big fallers in global stock market rout
item.description: Shares in Anthropic have fallen by more than 10% at Friday's open on Wall Street, just a day after their record-breaking Nasdaq debut, as part of a global stock market rout.

item.title: WATCH: Riverboat captain celebrates more than 50 years on the Mississippi River
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to riverboat captain Robbie Mitchell, who is marking a major milestone aboard the legendary steamboat Natchez.

item.title: WATCH: New video angle shows moment of Brooklyn apartment building's deadly collapse
item.description: Dash cam video from a bus passing by shows the terrifying moment a three-story Brooklyn apartment building buckled and crumbled to the ground, killing eight people and injuring multiple others.

item.title: WATCH: Grand Theft Auto VI is back and shattering records
item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.

item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.description: There are three other former soldiers who are on the military’s death row.

item.title: What Obama said to newly elected Democrats after midterm gains
item.description: Former President Barack Obama told Democratic U.S. House members-elect on Wednesday that they should value their ideological diversity even if they have disagreements.

item.title: Xi tells Trump US must do 'the right thing' over Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping used his meeting with President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday to warn against the creation of "turbulence" over the issue of Taiwan.

item.title: WATCH: Trump calls Putin, Xi his friends after meeting
item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.
